2.5.1.3-r1.burton_quote: hot medicines increase the disease by drying too much

2.5.1.3-r2.burton_quote: I never gave it (saith he) but after once or twice, by the help of God they were happily cured

2.5.1.3-r4.translation: That he had observed through long experience that melancholics can be excellently cured by it without harm. The same [author]: black hellebore, otherwise fearsome and dangerous, is made so fit for use with spirit of wine and oil that it can be given safely even to children.

2.5.1.3-r5.burton_quote: It is most certain (saith he) that the virtue of this herb is great, and admirable in effect, and little differing from Balm itself; and he that knows well how to make use of it, hath more art than all their books contain, or all the Doctors in Germany can show

2.5.1.3-r7.burton_quote: Put case (saith he) all other medicines fail, by the help of God this alone shall do it, and ’tis a crowned medicine which must be kept in secret

2.5.1.3-r8.burton_quote: will have 101 to be taken by three and three in like sort, which Salust. Salvian. approves de re med. lib. 2 cap. 1 with some of the same powder, till all be spent, a most excellent remedy for all melancholy and mad men
2.5.1.3-r8.translation: every morning let them take soft-boiled eggs, with the following powder sprinkled over the egg
